summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of psoriatic arthritis, morbid obesity, and recent MSSA abscess was admitted after presenting with confusion, vomiting, and acute renal failure with a peak creatinine of 8.1. He was found to have pre-renal azotemia due to dehydration, likely exacerbated by a rapid prednisone taper and concurrent use of HCTZ, leading to relative adrenal insufficiency. His mental status improved with IV fluids and doubling of his prednisone dose. Renal function returned to baseline, and he was weaned off antibiotics after cultures showed no infection. CK elevation resolved with rehydration, and atorvastatin was held. He was discharged home with instructions to slowly taper steroids, monitor hydration, and follow up with his primary care and rheumatology providers.
